question: So what's the difference between an OPD visit and an IPD one on the bill?
expected_answer: OPD (outpatient department) means you see a doctor and go home the same day without being admitted; IPD (inpatient department) means you are admitted and stay in a hospital bed, so IPD charges cover the room, nursing and treatment during the stay.

key_facts: OPD is outpatient: you are seen and go home without being admitted
IPD is inpatient: you are admitted and occupy a hospital bed

question: How much is an OPD visit with the heart specialist at Nashik?
expected_answer: A cardiology (super-specialist) consultation at the Nashik branch is ₹1,300, plus a one-time registration fee of ₹100 if it is your first visit there.

key_facts: super-specialist consultations (cardiology) at Nashik cost ₹1,300
one-time registration fee of ₹100 on the first visit

question: Can I just walk in to see the orthopaedic doctor at Baner?
expected_answer: Not at Baner: walk-in tokens there are issued only for general medicine and paediatrics (until 6:30 pm), so an orthopaedics consultation needs a prior appointment through the call centre, app or WhatsApp; a walk-in is offered the next available slot, which may be another day.
answer_aliases: no walk-in for specialists at Baner

key_facts: walk-in tokens are issued only for general medicine and paediatrics
Specialist and super-specialist consultations at Baner are by prior appointment only
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, you can walk in during OPD hours, take a token at reception and wait to see the orthopaedic doctor.

question: Can I bring my old reports and prescriptions to the follow-up, does it help?
expected_answer: Yes, please do: they let the doctor compare your earlier results with the new ones, see which medicines you have taken and how you responded, and avoid repeating tests unnecessarily.

key_facts: lets the doctor compare earlier and current results
shows past medicines and treatment, avoiding unnecessary repeat tests

question: My receipt says free follow-up, what does that mean, like for how long?
expected_answer: One follow-up visit with the same doctor at the same branch is free only within 5 days of your paid consultation (the day after counts as day 1); from day 6 the full consultation fee applies.

key_facts: a follow-up visit is free only within 5 days of the paid consultation
with the same doctor at the same branch
From day 6 onwards, the full consultation fee applies
meta.common_prior: A follow-up visit within 7 days (or up to 14-15 days) of the consultation is free.

question: If my family doctor gives me a referral letter, what's it for?
expected_answer: A referral letter is a note from your doctor to the specialist explaining why you are being referred, with your symptoms, history, current medicines and test results, so the specialist knows the background and what question to answer.
answer_aliases: a letter from one doctor to another

key_facts: a note from one doctor to another, usually a specialist
summarises the reason for referral, history, medicines and test results

question: If I cancel my appointment the night before, do I get a full refund?
expected_answer: No. The night before is within 24 hours of the slot, so a ₹200 cancellation fee is deducted from the refund; only cancellations made at least 24 hours ahead are refunded in full.

key_facts: If you cancel within 24 hours of the slot, a cancellation fee of ₹200 is deducted
free of charge up to 24 hours before your slot
meta.common_prior: Yes, you can cancel any time before the appointment and get a full refund.

question: How many hours after eating do you take the PP sugar sample?
expected_answer: Post-prandial (PP) sugar is measured 2 hours after you start your meal, so note the time you began eating and don't eat again in between.

key_facts: 2 hours after starting the meal

question: Uh, how many hours do I need to fast for the fasting sugar test?
expected_answer: A strict 12-hour fast is required (but not more than 14 hours), with only plain water allowed; with less than 12 hours the sugar is reported as a random sugar, not a fasting one.

key_facts: requires a strict 12-hour fast
Do not fast for more than 14 hours
you may drink plain water
meta.common_prior: At least 8 hours (8 to 10 hours) of fasting.

question: Um, how much is it for someone to come home and take my sample?
expected_answer: Home sample collection costs ₹250 per visit, and it's free when the test bill is ₹2,000 or more; book by 8:00 pm the day before.

key_facts: The home collection charge is ₹250 per visit
waived when the test bill is ₹2,000 or more

question: How long does the ECG part take, like the test itself?
expected_answer: A resting ECG takes only about five to ten minutes including setup; the recording itself lasts under a minute while you lie still with stickers on your chest, arms and legs, and it's painless.

key_facts: a resting ECG takes about five to ten minutes
painless; electrodes are placed on the chest, arms and legs

question: What's actually different between your basic and executive health checkups?
expected_answer: The Essential Health Check is ₹2,499 and covers routine blood and urine tests, chest X-ray and ECG; the Executive Health Check is ₹5,999, only at Baner, and adds a treadmill test (TMT), 2D echo, vitamin D and B12, ultrasound abdomen, lung function, eye and dental checks, with same-day reports and specialist consultations.

key_facts: Essential Health Check costs ₹2,499
Executive Health Check costs ₹5,999 and is available only at the Baner branch
adds a treadmill test (TMT), 2D echo, vitamin D, vitamin B12, ultrasound abdomen

question: And how long till we get the reports back?
expected_answer: For the Essential Health Check the full report is uploaded to the app within 48 hours of the visit, and the printed file can then be collected from the health check desk.

history.text: Hi, I want to book the basic health check for my father.
Sure, I can help with that. Which date works for him?
Saturday morning is available. He'll need to come in fasting.

key_facts: the full report is uploaded to the Varunika app within 48 hours of the visit

question: Yes, but what does cashless mean in practice, like who pays?
expected_answer: Cashless means the insurer, usually through its TPA, pays the approved hospital bill directly to the network hospital, so you don't pay the covered amount and claim it back later; you pay only what your policy doesn't cover.

history.text: My doctor says the surgery can be done on cashless.
Okay. Do you have your insurance card or e-card with you?

key_facts: the insurer or TPA settles the approved bill directly with the hospital
the patient pays only non-covered or non-payable items

question: If it's cashless, do I still pay anything when I get admitted?
expected_answer: Yes. Even with a cashless request, a refundable deposit of ₹10,000 is collected at admission; it's adjusted at discharge against non-payable items such as registration, consumables and attendant food, plus any co-payment.

key_facts: a refundable deposit of ₹10,000 is collected at admission
adjusted against non-payable items
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: No, with cashless the insurer pays the hospital directly, so you don't pay anything at admission.

question: How early do I send my insurance papers before my planned surgery?
expected_answer: The pre-authorisation request must be submitted at least 72 hours before the planned admission, with the policy card, the patient's photo ID, the doctor's admission advice with the estimate, and previous reports.

key_facts: the pre-authorisation request must be submitted at least 72 hours before the planned admission date

question: What's a TPA, and why's it involved in my insurance claim?
expected_answer: A TPA (third party administrator) is a licensed agency your insurer appoints to handle its claims; it issues the health card, processes cashless pre-authorisations and settles or reimburses claims on the insurer's behalf.

key_facts: TPA stands for third party administrator
processes claims and cashless approvals on behalf of the insurer

question: Why was the insurance desk shut when I came by on Sunday evening?
expected_answer: On Sundays the insurance and TPA desk is open only from 9:00 am to 2:00 pm (Monday to Saturday it's 8:00 am to 8:00 pm); emergency admissions after that are registered by Admissions and the cashless request is sent the next morning.

key_facts: Sunday 9:00 am to 2:00 pm
Monday to Saturday 8:00 am to 8:00 pm
the cashless request is sent the next morning

question: So why do you need a photo ID for my seventy-year-old dad's admission?
expected_answer: A photo ID confirms the patient's identity so records, test results and treatment are matched to the right person, and it is needed for billing, insurance claims and any legal or medico-legal paperwork.

key_facts: verifies the patient's identity for accurate, safe records and treatment
needed for billing, insurance and legal records

question: So how much deposit do we pay on the day of admission?
expected_answer: For a single room the admission deposit for a self-paying patient is ₹50,000.

history.text: My mother is getting admitted on Monday, the doctor wants her under observation.
Alright. Will you be using insurance, or paying yourselves?
We're paying ourselves, and we'd like a single room.
Okay, single rooms are available for Monday.

key_facts: single room ₹50,000

question: When is the extra deposit paid back, like at discharge itself?
expected_answer: Not at the discharge counter: the excess deposit is refunded only by bank transfer (or to the original card) within 10 working days of the final bill being settled, after you submit the refund form with a cancelled cheque.

key_facts: the excess is not paid back in cash at the discharge counter
refunded only by bank transfer
within 10 working days of the final bill being settled
meta.common_prior: The excess deposit is refunded at the billing counter at discharge, the same day.

question: They said we'll get a discharge summary, um, what is that exactly?
expected_answer: A discharge summary is the doctor's written record of the hospital stay: the diagnosis, treatment and procedures done, condition at discharge, medicines to continue and follow-up instructions; keep it for future doctors and insurance claims.

history.text: My father is getting discharged tomorrow.
Okay, the ward team will start the process after the doctor's morning round.

key_facts: written summary of the hospital stay: diagnosis, treatment and procedures
lists medicines to continue and follow-up instructions

question: Why was half a day's room rent added to dad's final bill?
expected_answer: The room has to be vacated by 2:00 pm on the day of discharge; leaving after 2:00 pm adds half a day's room rent (after 8:00 pm, a full day's rent), so he most likely left the room after 2:00 pm.

key_facts: the room must be vacated by 2:00 pm on the day of discharge
after 2:00 pm, half a day's room rent is added

question: Do visitors really have to sanitise their hands before going into the ward at Baner?
expected_answer: Yes. Hand hygiene stops visitors carrying germs in to patients, many of whom have weak immunity or wounds, and it also protects visitors from picking up infections in the hospital.

key_facts: prevents spreading infection to vulnerable patients
also protects the visitor

question: Can I bring my kids along when we visit their grandma in the ward?
expected_answer: Only if they are 12 or older: children under 12 are not allowed into wards, private rooms or ICUs; they can meet her only in the ground-floor family lounge between 5:00 pm and 6:00 pm, and only if the treating team allows her to come down.

key_facts: children under 12 are not allowed into wards, private rooms or ICUs
family lounge on the ground floor, between 5:00 pm and 6:00 pm
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, children can visit with an adult during normal visiting hours.

question: What are the evening visiting hours for the general ward at Baner?
expected_answer: Evening visiting for general wards and private rooms is 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm (mornings are 11:00 am to 12:00 pm); ICU visiting is only 4:00 pm to 4:30 pm.
answer_aliases: five to seven in the evening

key_facts: 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm

question: What's the point of an authorisation letter if my brother collects my file?
expected_answer: Medical records are confidential, so the letter is your written consent that this particular person may receive them on your behalf; it protects your privacy and lets the hospital release the records properly.

key_facts: medical records are confidential
the letter is the patient's written consent for that person to collect them

question: How long until I can collect copies of my mom's hospital file?
expected_answer: Certified copies of an inpatient case file are released only after 15 working days from the date of the written request; they can't be fast-tracked, and the fee is ₹500 for up to 50 pages.

key_facts: released only after 15 working days from the date of the written request
requests cannot be fast-tracked
meta.common_prior: Within 72 hours, or a few working days, of the request.

question: Can the doctor examine me properly on a video consultation?
expected_answer: Only partly: on video the doctor can take your history, look at visible things such as a rash and review reports, but can't do a hands-on examination like listening to your chest or feeling your abdomen, so you may be asked to come in person.

key_facts: no hands-on physical examination over video
the doctor can still take a history, look at visible signs and review reports

question: What happens if the doctor doesn't show up on my video call?
expected_answer: If the doctor hasn't joined within 15 minutes of the slot time, you can choose a full refund, credited within 3 working days, or a free rebooking.

key_facts: If the doctor has not joined within 15 minutes of the slot time
full refund, credited within 3 working days, or a free rebooking
